court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Abhinay Gyan Gangeshwar Prasad Thr. His ... vs State Of Mah. Thr. Ps Incharge Rana ...

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Mr. Abhinav Gyan S/o Gangeshwar : PETITIONER, husband
parties.respondent_defendant: 1. State of Maharashtra, Through Police : Station Incharge, Rana Pratap Nagar, Nagpur Tahsil & District - Nagpur (Maharashtra State), 2. Mrs. Anupriya D/o Anjani Sharan RESPONDENTS (Mrs. Anupriya W/o Abhinav Gyan Prasad), wife

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner is seeking a writ of habeas corpus for direction to respondents, particularly respondent No.2 to produce minor child born out of the marriage between petitioner (husband) and respondent No.2 (wife). Minor child is a citizen of USA.

legal_principles.principle: The welfare and best interests of the child are the bedrock on which petitions like the present petition ought to be decided.
legal_principles.held: On this basis, it was submitted that the writ petition deserved to be allowed.

legal_principles.principle: Merely because there was an order passed against the respondent No.2, by a Court of foreign jurisdiction, that in itself would not render illegal the custody of the minor child with the respondent No.2.
legal_principles.held: This hit at the very root of the matter, demonstrating that no circumstances exist for this Court to invoke the writ of habeas corpus in the present case.
cited_cases: settled law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court

legal_principles.principle: Removing a child from his settled surroundings would prejudicially affect his welfare.
legal_principles.held: It was submitted that removing him from such surroundings would prejudicially affect his welfare, thereby indicating that the writ petition deserved to be dismissed on this count also.

outcome.final_order: Direction for handing over the minor child to the petitioner for being taken back to the United States of America (USA).
